title: Call to action
subtitle: The band that closes a page: a heading, a supporting line and one button.

tutorial.p: A Call to action goes at the end of a page and points the reader to what to look at next. Examples are the careers site and the list of press releases. It has a heading, a supporting line and one button.

ul: the end of Careers: pointing to the careers site
the end of every press release (the Single Posts template), for example this press release
the page shown for an address that does not exist (the Page: 404 template)

steps.text: Open the + (block inserter) at the top left, type call to action in the search field and click Call to action. You can also type /cta in the page.
steps.alt: The block inserter searched for call to action, with the Call to action tile outlined in red

steps.text: The placeholders Call to action heading, Supporting line and Button label appear. Click each one and type.
steps.alt: A Call to action just added, with the placeholders Call to action heading, Supporting line and Button label and the toolbar above

steps.text: The band with its text filled in. In the editor the button runs the full width of the band. On the site at desktop width it sits to the right of the text.
steps.alt: A Call to action filled in: a heading, a supporting line and a button whose arrow points out of a box

steps.text: Save the page (Mac: Command + S, Windows: Ctrl + S).

tutorial.p: A button with text but no address still shows on the site, and does nothing when clicked. A link to another website opens in a new tab.

steps.text: Click Button link in the toolbar, type the address and press Enter. The link appears under the field.
steps.alt: The window Button link opens, with the address that was set and the icons Edit link, Remove link and Copy link below it

steps.text: To open it in a new tab, click the pencil icon (Edit link). Open Advanced if it is closed, tick Open in new tab and click Apply. The button's arrow changes to one pointing out of a box.
steps.alt: The field Edit link opens, with Open in new tab ticked under Advanced, and the Cancel and Apply buttons

steps.text: Click H2 in the toolbar to choose H2, H3 or H4 as the heading level.
steps.alt: The list Change level opens from the toolbar: Heading 2, Heading 3 and Heading 4, with Heading 2 selected

steps.text: To give the band an ID, open Advanced in the sidebar and type in HTML anchor. It is the only panel in the sidebar.
steps.alt: The Advanced panel in the sidebar, with the HTML anchor and Additional CSS class fields

steps.text: Save the page (Mac: Command + S, Windows: Ctrl + S).

tutorial.p: A pattern is a way to add a block with sample text already in it. The Call to action pattern adds the band with the Career Opportunities & Open Positions heading, a line pointing to the careers site, and a Careers Site button. For a careers band, start from it rather than writing the text from nothing. To decide the heading and text yourself, build from an empty band as above.

Clicking a band added from the pattern selects the whole pattern, and it cannot be changed as it is. To change its text or settings, click Edit pattern, and click Exit pattern when you finish. The change applies to this page only.

steps.text: In the + (block inserter) at the top left, open the Patterns tab and type call to action in the search field. The Call to action pattern is the preview on the left (outlined in red).
steps.alt: The block inserter's Patterns tab searched for call to action. The Call to action preview on the left is outlined in red

steps.text: Click the band that was added, and the sidebar shows the pattern's name and description. Click Edit pattern.
steps.alt: The sidebar with the Call to action pattern selected: its name, its description and the Edit pattern button

steps.text: The bar at the top reads "Back Call to action · Pattern", and the blocks inside can be edited. Rewrite the heading and text.
steps.alt: The bar at the top of the screen: Back Call to action · Pattern

steps.text: When you finish, click Exit pattern in the sidebar.
steps.alt: The sidebar while the pattern is being edited, with the Exit pattern button

steps.text: Save the page (Mac: Command + S, Windows: Ctrl + S).

tutorial.h3: Checking it in the Site Editor

tutorial.p: The band at the end of each press release is a pattern called Press release call to action, placed by the theme in the Single Posts and Page: 404 templates. Its text is set by the theme, so ask the site team to change it.

steps.text: Open Appearance → Editor, choose Templates and open Single Posts (outlined in red).
steps.alt: The template list in the Site Editor, with Single Posts outlined in red

steps.text: Open List View and select Press release call to action, below Content. It sits between the content and the footer.
steps.alt: The Single Posts template in the Site Editor, with Press release call to action selected from List View

tutorial.p: The toolbar and the sidebar show Edit pattern. Do not click it. It opens the band for editing, and saving afterwards changes the band on every press release. If you click it by mistake, click Exit pattern and close without saving.
None. No other block can go inside the band.

examples.p: As on Careers. It opens another website in a new tab.

examples.block: <!-- wp:my-theme/cta {"title":"Careers and open positions","body":"For current openings and how to apply, please visit our careers site.","buttonText":"Careers site","buttonUrl":"https://careers.example.com/","buttonOpensInNewTab":true} /-->

examples.p: The button's arrow points straight ahead.

examples.block: <!-- wp:my-theme/cta {"title":"Latest press releases","body":"The latest news and information about our activities.","buttonText":"View all press releases","buttonUrl":"{site}/newsroom/"} /-->

examples.h3: A long heading and supporting line

examples.block: <!-- wp:my-theme/cta {"title":"For questions about the business and services of Example Securities, please contact our enquiries desk","body":"Our staff answer questions on weekdays from 9:00 to 17:00. Depending on the question, a reply may take some time.","buttonText":"Go to the enquiries desk","buttonUrl":"{site}/company-profile/"} /-->

steps.step: Add the block and save it
steps.alt: The field Edit link opens, with Open in new tab ticked under Advanced, and the Cancel and Apply buttons
instructions: Create a new page and close Choose a pattern.
Add a Call to action block with + or /cta.
Fill in the heading, the supporting line and the button label.
Save the draft (Mac: Command + S, Windows: Ctrl + S).
Reload the page (Mac: Command + R, Windows: Ctrl + R).
expected: With Open in new tab set, the button's arrow changes to one pointing out of a box.
After the reload your text is still there, with no "Block contains unexpected or invalid content." message.

instructions: Change the heading and the supporting line.
Set the heading to H3 in the toolbar.
Change Button link to /uat-en/newsroom/ and untick Open in new tab.
Save the draft (Mac: Command + S, Windows: Ctrl + S).
Reload the page (Mac: Command + R, Windows: Ctrl + R).
expected: H2, H3 and H4 are the only levels offered.
The button's arrow goes back to a straight arrow.
After the reload every change is still there.

steps.alt: The sidebar with the Call to action pattern selected: its name, its description and the Edit pattern button
instructions: Create a new page and close Choose a pattern.
Search for call to action and add the Call to action pattern under the tile.
Click Edit pattern, rewrite the heading, then click Exit pattern.
Save the draft (Mac: Command + S, Windows: Ctrl + S).
Reload the page (Mac: Command + R, Windows: Ctrl + R).
expected: A band with the Career Opportunities & Open Positions heading, a line of text and a Careers Site button is added.
After the reload the new heading is still there, with no "Block contains unexpected or invalid content." message.

steps.step: In Appearance → Editor → Templates, open Single Posts and find Press release call to action in List View. Do not click Edit pattern.
steps.expected: It sits below Content and above the footer, and reads Latest press releases.

steps.step: Go back without saving and open the Page: 404 template.
steps.expected: The same band sits below the page-not-found message.
